metadata.title: [CHORE]: MANIFEST.in includes files that should not ship in sdist/wheel
metadata.author: jonpspri

description:
## Summary

`MANIFEST.in` currently includes many build-time, infrastructure, and development-only files that should not be published in the Python source distribution (sdist) or wheel. These bloat the package, increase supply-chain surface, and may expose CI/CD or local-development artifacts to PyPI consumers.

## Files that likely should NOT be included

### Container / build files
- `Containerfile` (all variants) — These are Docker/Podman build recipes. They are not needed at runtime and should live only in the git repo.
- `Dockerfile` (if present) — Same rationale.

### Rust workspace files
- `Cargo.lock`
- `Cargo.toml`
- `rust-toolchain.toml`
These are build-time dependencies for the optional Rust extensions. They are irrelevant to the pure-Python wheel and should not be shipped in the Python package.

### Development / lint configuration
- `tox.ini` — Development-only testing tool.
- `.env.make`, `.env.example` — Local development environment templates.
- `.interrogaterc`, `.jshintrc`, `.htmlhintrc`, `.pycodestyle`, `.pylintc*`, `.flake8`, `.coveragerc`, `.yamllint`, `.editorconfig`, `.snyk`, `.darglint`, `.whitesource`, `whitesource.config`
These are tooling configs for local development and CI; they have no purpose in a published package.

### CI/CD and repo metadata
- `.dockerignore` — Docker build context exclusion file; irrelevant in a Python package.
- `CLAUDE.*`, `llms-full.txt`, `AGENTS.md` — AI-assistant / repo-local guidance; not package content.

### Other questionable inclusions
- `__init__` — Appears to be an empty sentinel file; verify if setuptools actually needs this.
- `gunicorn.config.py` — Runtime configuration for a specific WSGI server. If users need this, it should be documented as an example, not shipped as package data.
- `alembic.ini` — Alembic migration configuration. May be needed for CLI usage, but verify whether it should be package data vs. an example file.

## Why this matters

1. **Package bloat** — Every file in the sdist/wheel is downloaded by every consumer. Containerfiles and Rust lock files can be hundreds of KB.
2. **Supply-chain hygiene** — Publishing build recipes and CI configs increases the attack surface and may leak internal infrastructure details.
3. **PyPI policy alignment** — PyPI discourages shipping development artifacts in distributions.

## Suggested approach

1. Audit every `include` / `recursive-include` line in `MANIFEST.in` against the question: *"Does a user installing `pip install mcpgateway` need this file at runtime?"*
2. Remove anything that is build-time, dev-time, or CI-time only.
3. Ensure `check-manifest` passes after cleanup.
4. Verify the wheel still contains everything needed for the application to start (templates, static assets, alembic migrations if CLI-managed, JSON schemas, etc.).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `check-manifest` passes cleanly.
- [ ] The wheel/sdist does not contain any `Containerfile*`, `Dockerfile*`, `Cargo.*`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, or development lint config files.
- [ ] The application can still start and serve the Admin UI from a `pip install` of the built wheel.
- [ ] A brief rationale is documented (either in `MANIFEST.in` comments or in this issue) for each category of included files.

## Related

- [MAINTENANCE] General dependency and packaging hygiene

comments.body:
Hey, I came across your project and checked out some of the infrastructure/backend setup you’re working on. I mainly help developers test backend reliability, deployment flow, API behavior, auth systems, scaling issues, edge-case failures, and launch readiness before production release.

If you ever need another technical eye for testing or infrastructure validation during launch stages, I’d be interested in helping out. Your project looks promising.
